title: Devlens Analysis: Who is hiring in the development sector this week
excerpt: 70 open roles, up from 46. Cox's Bazar and international NGOs still dominate, while two microfinance NGOs are recruiting for 2,262 posts.

image.alt: Graphic illustration by Devlens: a grid of grey and dark squares with a cluster of green squares

content:
DEVLENS ANALYSIS · Jobs market · 13 November 2026

Each week, Devlens looks at the numbers behind the sector. This week: the 70 development and humanitarian roles open on the Devlens jobs board on 13 November 2026, compared with the 46 we counted on 10 November. The board lists vacancies from UN agencies, international and national NGOs, donors and research centres, checked against each employer's own advert. It does not cover every vacancy in Bangladesh, so read these figures as a snapshot of the roles we track, not a census.

More listings, but read the rise with care

The board grew from 46 to 70 open roles in three days. Thirty-one new roles were added, five expired and one duplicate listing was merged. But much of the increase comes from where we looked, not only from more hiring. This week we added Helvetas procurement circulars, more UN listings and Bangla newspaper circulars to our regular search. A rise in our count is not, on its own, evidence that the job market is recovering.

Where the jobs are

Cox's Bazar's share fell from 39% to 30%, but only because Dhaka listings grew faster; the number of Cox's Bazar roles rose from 18 to 21. The Rohingya response is still the single biggest source of field jobs on the board. The International Rescue Committee alone accounts for 16 roles, 14 of them in Cox's Bazar.

Who is hiring

International NGOs post six in ten listings. Research centres grew quickly this week, led by five roles each at icddr,b and CIMMYT, the maize and wheat research centre. The EU Delegation is hiring for two posts.

The biggest hiring is not on the job portals

National NGOs account for only four listings. Counted by headcount, though, they dwarf everyone else. Two NGOs that run large microfinance programmes have published mass recruitment circulars: the Society for Social Service (SSS) is hiring for 1,782 posts in 17 job categories, and People Oriented Program Implementation (POPI) for 480 posts in five categories across 23 districts. Together that is 2,262 vacancies, far more than all the other roles on the board combined.

These circulars appear in Bangla newspapers and on the NGOs' own websites, not on the international portals most job seekers check. They also fit a pattern the Bangladesh Institute of Development Studies described last month: as foreign grants fall, lending is the part of NGO work that keeps growing. Read today's Devlens Special on NGO financing.

What kind of work

Health more than doubled, from 7 to 17 roles, with new posts at icddr,b, FHI 360, Ipas, Noora Health and The Fred Hollows Foundation. That fits the measles and dengue outbreaks and the BIDS finding that health was the only major aid sector to grow in 2025. Climate, gender and education roles remain scarce, even in a week when Bangladesh is pressing for adaptation finance at COP31.

Who can apply, and by when

  • 14 roles are for Bangladeshi nationals only, up from 11.
  • 10 roles are consultancies or requests for proposals, five of them from Helvetas.
  • 43 roles have no fixed deadline. Apply early: employers can close them without notice.

Of the 27 roles with a fixed deadline, 16 close within a week. Check the closing soon list every few days.

What it tells us

  • The Rohingya response still anchors field hiring, even as its funding falls. Many Cox's Bazar contracts run only to December or March.
  • Health is where new roles are appearing, driven by outbreaks and by health being the one aid sector that grew.
  • The largest numbers of jobs are at microfinance NGOs, advertised in Bangla rather than on international portals. Job seekers who search only in English miss most of them.
  • Climate and gender roles stay rare on the board, despite the attention both get in strategies and at COP31.

How we counted

All open roles listed on the Devlens jobs board on 13 November 2026, after removing expired listings. One recruitment that appeared twice (SSS, 1,782 posts) is counted once. Each mass recruitment circular counts as one role in the tables. Employer type is based on the hiring organisation; international NGOs include country offices of organisations headquartered abroad, such as Islamic Relief Bangladesh and Helvetas. Locations follow the employer's advert. The 10 November figures come from last week's snapshot. Employers can send us vacancies to list for free. Image: a graphic illustration by Devlens Bangladesh.
